intro: Every practice on the calendar, and every practice on its own page. The number is what carries the teaching order — a rainout moves the whole schedule down one instead of skipping it — and the date is only where that number happens to land. Built one practice at a time: nothing gets installed before its prerequisite is in place.

preseason.label: Before the first game
preseason.note: Alignment first, plays second — every kid knows his spot and we count seven on the line before anybody touches the ball. A formation run without thinking beats six plays half known.

season.label: Once the season starts
season.note: One new look at a time, and only once the last one has hurt somebody. Each exists because a defence started cheating something — not worth installing before that happens.

practices.focus: Line up in the Regular I
practices.emphasis: Install the formation itself — alignment only, no plays. Every kid knows his spot, and we count seven on the line every single snap until it is boring.
practices.finisher: First unit vs. second unit sprint relay race.

practices.focus: Line up in the Regular I again
practices.emphasis: The same formation install. Reps on alignment and the seven-on-the-line count until they can do it without thinking — then we are ready to hand somebody the ball.
practices.finisher: First unit vs. second unit sprint relay race.

practices.emphasis: Two runs, two different jobs. Dive hits fast off the double team before the linebackers can read it — snap to handoff under a second. Wedge is short yardage: nobody blocks a man, the whole line squeezes to the center's back and pushes. Same formation, same snap count — first time somebody besides the coach is naming who gets the ball.
practices.finisher: First unit vs. second unit sprint relay race.

practices.focus: Go live and set the first team
agility_drills: Warm-ups — lap, dynamic stretch, form running (10 min)
Station 1 — tackling: approach, break down, wrap and drive (15 min)
Station 2 — blocking: fit, hands inside, drive the feet (15 min)
Two groups, swap on the whistle — every kid does both stations
practices.emphasis: No new install. Everything we already have — Dive and Wedge, both ways out of the Regular I — goes live for the rest of practice, and the point is personnel, not plays. Run the same handful over and over against a real look and watch who moves people, who finds the hole without being told and who tackles in space. Nobody gets a spot on reputation: the kid who does it live is the kid who starts.
practices.huddle: Name the first team out loud, and the first sub at every spot.

practices.focus: Fundamentals both ways, Power and Toss, live scrimmage

drills: Getting into and out of the huddle

blocks.title: Offensive install
notes: Rotating through the first, second, third and fourth units
In and out of the huddle

practices.huddle: Review what we did today at practice.

practices.focus: Split Backs: slot sweep and TE sweep
practices.emphasis: One long block after the warm-up. Review #17 and #18, then install the sweeps: #23 and #24 (slot sweep) and #25 and #26 (TE sweep). The runner stays down until the snap, comes across, takes the handoff at full speed, and turns up behind the halfbacks.

blocks.title: Warm-up
blocks.note: Five minutes, moving the whole time.

blocks.title: Split Backs install
notes: One group, the rest of practice
#17 and #18 first, then #23 and #24 (Z Sweep both ways), then #25 and #26 (X Sweep Right, Y Sweep Left)
In and out of the huddle every rep. Z Right or Z Left, then the number and the word -- and on a letter call the way it goes, last

practices.huddle: #23 and #24 are the slot sweep -- he lines up one way and runs the other, which is why the call ends with the way. #25 is X Sweep Right, #26 is Y Sweep Left. Stay down, come across, handoff at full speed.

practices.focus: Split Backs: 19 Fake Sweep, plus Tuesday's sweeps
practices.emphasis: One long block after the warm-up. Review Tuesday — #17, #18, the slot sweep and the TE sweep — then install #21, Z Left 19 Fake Sweep. Fake the handoff to the right halfback, then the quarterback keeps it left behind the left halfback.

blocks.title: Warm-up
blocks.note: Five minutes, moving the whole time.

blocks.title: Split Backs install
notes: One group, the rest of practice
In and out of the huddle every rep. Z Right or Z Left, then the number and the word -- and on a letter call the way it goes, last

practices.huddle: #21 is 19 Fake Sweep. Fake to the right halfback, keep it left.

practices.focus: Everybody somewhere new: rotate the six skill spots
practices.emphasis: No new play tonight. Everything already in the book is fair game -- Regular I and Split Backs -- and what changes every snap is who is standing where. Get the calls right with the first eleven first; the lineup does not start moving until they are.

blocks.title: Warm-up
blocks.note: Five minutes, moving the whole time.

blocks.title: Go back through the base playbook, and rotate through it
notes: First time through with the first eleven, no rotating -- the calls have to be right before the lineup starts moving
Coach calls off the installed book, Regular I and Split Backs, mixing it up as we go
In and out of the huddle every rep
blocks.note: Two carousels turning at once. The ends walk down the list -- whoever was at Y goes to X and the next boy comes in at Y. The backs turn the other way, and the slot is the door the other five walk through. One row a snap, read left to right; the small number is where he sits on the depth chart at that spot, so a 1 is his own spot and anything higher is a boy getting a look at somebody else's. The card says who, not what -- the call comes from the coach on the snap. Run the six, go back to the top, run them again -- twelve snaps, and every boy gets at least two at the spot that is really his.

blocks.title: Defense
blocks.note: Line up in the 4-4, our everyday front, and count it out loud: four down, four backers, two corners and the free safety. Same rule as the offense had in August -- everybody knows his spot before anybody chases the ball.

blocks.title: Relay race
blocks.note: First unit vs. second unit sprint relay race.

practices.huddle: Nobody owns a spot. Everybody played somewhere new tonight, and the boy beside you can do your job -- that is what makes a Saturday survivable when somebody is out. Name the spot you liked best on the way to the car.
